$snippetComment: The markdown demo's fixtures. AN ENUM, NOT A TEXT BOX, and the deferred entry below explains what stays deferred and why. Each snippet is chosen for a BRANCH of the pipeline a published article cannot show you: a published article is by definition one that tripped none of the refusals. Expected values are hand-written from the pipeline's rules and never captured from a run, hard rule 10's fixture independence: `toc` is the heading slugs in order, `blockedCount` is how many URLs the protocol allowlist demotes, and `throws` says whether renderBody refuses the snippet outright. A snippet must cite no media, and the demo hands the renderer an image resolver that throws, so a snippet that grows an image citation fails loudly rather than reaching for a bucket from a public page.

markdownSnippets.label: Headings and code
markdownSnippets.note: The ordinary path. Every heading is slugged and collected into the table of contents in document order, which is the same list a post's sidebar is built from, and the code block is highlighted on the server by the same grammar the articles use.

$cookiePresetComment: The theme demo's presets, and the gate's behavioural fixtures. EVERY EXPECTED ANSWER IS HAND-WRITTEN from the rules in app/lib/theme.ts, never captured from a run: hard rule 10's fixture independence, the same bargain the swatches and the key presets make. `attribute` is the data-theme value or null for the absence that hands the decision to prefers-color-scheme. The set covers every BRANCH rather than being long: both writable values, the legacy value that is honoured as the no-cookie path, no cookie at all, a theme cookie sitting among unrelated ones, the malformed percent-escape that used to throw a URIError on every page for that reader, and a value nothing writes.

cookiePresets.label: A reader who chose dark
cookiePresets.note: One of the two values the endpoint accepts, because the control posts the theme it is switching TO and that is only ever light or dark.

cookiePresets.label: A reader who chose light
cookiePresets.note: The other writable value. The attribute is written into the first byte of HTML, so the server never has to correct itself.

cookiePresets.label: Nobody has chosen
cookiePresets.note: The default branch, not a fallback. The attribute is ABSENT, which is what hands the decision to prefers-color-scheme, and the meta says the document supports both because asserting one would be claiming a choice nobody made.

cookiePresets.label: A legacy cookie from the three-button control
cookiePresets.note: The control could write this and those cookies live in readers' browsers for a year, which is the max-age. It resolves exactly as no cookie does, so the two readers converge on one cache entry and one document rather than on two that happen to look alike.

cookiePresets.label: Among other cookies
cookiePresets.note: The header is split and walked, so position does not matter. Worth seeing because the presence of ANY cookie, not this one, is what downgrades a response to private on the wire.

cookiePresets.label: A malformed percent escape
cookiePresets.note: Decoding this raises a URIError. Nothing this site writes can produce it, but a cookie is client state: hand-edited, truncated by a proxy, corrupted in storage. It was unguarded until a test found it, and the throw landed on the cache-key path, which made it a server error on every page for that reader until they found and cleared a cookie nothing told them about.

cookiePresets.label: A value nothing writes
cookiePresets.note: Junk and the legacy value take the same road: anything outside the writable set falls to the default rather than throwing, because a bad cookie should cost a reader the default theme and never the page.

$keyPresetComment: The key demo's presets, and the gate's behavioural fixtures. EVERY EXPECTED ANSWER HERE IS HAND-WRITTEN from the grammar in app/lib/media/classify.mjs, never captured from a run of it: hard rule 10's fixture independence, the same rule that keeps scripts/fixtures/icon-suite.json out of the generator's hands. check:features runs the real parsers over each key and compares. `dimensions` is a `<w>x<h>` string or null, `digest` is the sixteen hex digits or null, and `kind` is the classifier's kind or the literal "refused" for a key whose extension it throws on. The set is chosen to cover every BRANCH rather than to be long: both content-key forms, the leading-zero dimension the collapsing differential caught, a /media/ path carrying a transform query, an og/ derived key, a brand asset, and an extension the classifier refuses.

keyPresets.label: An uploaded raster
keyPresets.note: The ordinary shape: the site prefix, sixteen hex digits of the content digest, the intrinsic dimensions, the extension. An upload with a usable filename also carries a slug of it between the prefix and the digest.

keyPresets.label: A vector, which has no pixel size
keyPresets.note: No dimension segment, because an SVG has no intrinsic pixel size and a zero would be a measurement rather than the absence of one.

keyPresets.label: A leading zero in the dimension
keyPresets.note: Refused outright. A deleted reader spelled this axis loosely and answered 800 by 600 for this key while the other two readers were calling it not a content key at all. One key, three readers, two answers.

keyPresets.label: A served path with a transform on it
keyPresets.note: Three different contracts, visible at once. The two extracting readers accept a path and strip the query, because a width is a transform request rather than a different object. The boolean documents a BARE key and refuses a leading slash. And the classifier takes a path or a key, never a URL: it reads everything after the last dot, so the extension here is webp-question-mark-w-equals-320, which is in no table and refuses. Every caller in the codebase hands it an object key or a static path, so the boundary is a contract rather than a defect, and this is the only place you can see it.

keyPresets.label: A generated social card
keyPresets.note: The regenerable tier, told apart by prefix because that is what the writer controls. Losing one is an inconvenience rather than a loss.

keyPresets.label: The site mark
keyPresets.note: Brand rather than icon, and the test is who fetches it: an icon is declared to the platform and fetched without this code being involved, a brand asset is named by a module.

keyPresets.label: An extension nobody has classified
keyPresets.note: The classifier throws rather than returning a default, which is the whole reason it is a function and not a lookup: a new file type has to stop a build instead of acquiring a plausible kind nobody chose.

$swatchComment: Ratified palette pairs the contrast lab opens on, and the gate's behavioural fixtures. A pair here that the page does not render, or a preset on the page that is not here, fails reconciliation.

deferred.reason: Narrowed rather than closed on 2026-08-30. The FIXED-SNIPPET form shipped as a demo above, which was never what this entry was refusing: the reason has always been arbitrary text into a syntax highlighter running on a WebAssembly regex engine and into a directive layer that resolves assets, which is a compute and sanitization surface needing its own threat model. An enum of committed snippets opens none of that and shows the branches a published article cannot, because a published article is by definition one that tripped none of the refusals. A text box still needs the threat model.
